data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"An epistemic, data-centric protocol using a distributed Merkle witness tree shifts safety from process liveness to content acknowledgment; the exact durable records are Merkle roots and inclusion proofs.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Requires a distributed witness layer with its own fault assumptions","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Inclusion proof generation latency may delay completion indefinitely","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Without witnesses, no evidence can ever be declared complete, causing workspace accumulation","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Rather than tracking process liveness, the protocol requires that any completed evidence be hashed and that hash inserted into a Merkle tree witnessed by multiple observers. Reclamation performs a 'corpse examination': it hashes the orphaned workspace and checks inclusion in the Merkle tree. If present, evidence is completed and must not be displaced. If absent, reclamation proceeds. The causal mechanism shifts from process-centric to data-centric: a workspace is safe not because its creator is alive but because its content is globally acknowledged. Adjudication: where evidence shows observer crash rates are lower than process crash rates, this is safer than lease protocols; where observers are unavailable, it degrades to no reclamation, analogous to the log protocol's stall but with stronger tamper evidence.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
